## Course description

**Data Description** introduces the basic statistical tools corresponding to the
first stage of data analysis: numerical summaries and graphical representation
of data, computed hands-on in Excel. By the end of the course, you will be able
to take a raw column of business data — sales, weather, customer counts — and
turn it into frequency tables, charts, and summary indicators that support a real
business decision. A single running case study, **"The Wandering Fork"** (a
fictional food-truck business), carries every worked example from Module 2 onward,
so results build on each other across the whole course.

The course has **10 modules of 3 hours** (30 contact hours). Each module follows
the same pattern: a business question; concrete activities on a few numbers you
compute by hand, *before* any formula; a notation decoder that reads every
formula aloud and links each symbol to those numbers; a worked example on the
shared dataset; a short derivation; exercises by hand with collapsible
solutions; common mistakes; a short exit check; and an **Excel lab done as
homework** at the end of the module page, so class time goes to concepts,
notation and practice. Modules 1–5 still include their original in-class Excel
lab.

## Curriculum placement

This course is the natural sequel to **Mathematical Fundamentals
(MS01,** [`teaching/mathematical-fundamentals/`](../mathematical-fundamentals/index.qmd)**)**
and **Mathematical Analysis (MS02,**
[`teaching/mathematical-analysis/`](../mathematical-analysis/index.qmd)**)**,
and it is itself the prerequisite refresher for **Inferential
Statistics (MS04,**
[`teaching/decision-making-stat/`](../decision-making-stat/index.qmd)**)**,
whose own Session 6 explicitly revisits the numerical summaries
introduced here before moving on to confidence intervals and
hypothesis testing.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this course, you will be able to:

1. Identify the type and level of measurement of a variable and say
   which summaries it allows (Module 1).
2. Build the right frequency table and chart for a qualitative or a
   quantitative variable, by hand in class and in Excel with
   `COUNTIFS`, PivotTables and charts (Modules 2–3).
3. Compute and interpret central tendency, position, dispersion and
   shape, by hand in class and in Excel at home with `AVERAGE`,
   `MEDIAN`, `QUARTILE.EXC`, `STDEV.S` and `SKEW` (Modules 4–7).
4. Build and read a contingency table and a scatter plot for two
   variables observed together (Module 8).
5. Compute and interpret covariance, correlation and a simple linear
   regression line, by hand in class and in Excel at home with
   `CORREL`, `SLOPE`, `INTERCEPT` and `RSQ` (Module 9).
6. Run a complete descriptive analysis of a new dataset and explain
   it to a business audience (Module 10).

|---|---|---|---|---:|
| I. Organising data | 1 | [Module 1](modules/module-01.qmd) | What is statistics? Data types and measurement | 3 |
| I. Organising data | 2 | [Module 2](modules/module-02.qmd) | Organising qualitative data: frequency tables and charts | 3 |
| I. Organising data | 3 | [Module 3](modules/module-03.qmd) | Organising quantitative data: histograms and cumulative curves | 3 |
| II. Summarising one variable | 4 | [Module 4](modules/module-04.qmd) | Measures of central tendency | 3 |
| II. Summarising one variable | 5 | [Module 5](modules/module-05.qmd) | Measures of position: quartiles, percentiles, boxplot | 3 |
| II. Summarising one variable | 6 | [Module 6](modules/module-06.qmd) | Measures of dispersion: variance, standard deviation, CV | 3 |
| II. Summarising one variable | 7 | [Module 7](modules/module-07.qmd) | Shape of distributions and univariate review | 3 |

**Part I** — Organising data (Modules 1–3, 9h) · **Part II** —

**Reference pages:** the [dataset](modules/dataset.qmd) (download the

## Assessment

| Examination | % of overall grade | Assessment mode | Duration | Covers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Midterm Exam (ME) | 35% | Individual written, MCQ component | 45 min | Modules 1–5 |
| Final Exam (FE) | 65% | Individual written, MCQ component | 90 min | Modules 1–10 |

[Module 10](modules/module-10.qmd) closes the course with an original
mock exam in the same format; each solution names the module to
revise.

## Personal work

**Volume**: 20 hours. Complete the exercises associated with each
part of the course (Organising Data, Summarising One Variable,
Two Variables and Synthesis) between modules — every module page's
collapsible exercises are designed for exactly this.

Each module from Module 6 onward ends with an **Excel homework** (about
50–60 minutes), debriefed during the first 10 minutes of the next
module (Module 10's homework is a self-check against the solutions on
the page). That is about 5 of the 20 hours; the rest is by-hand revision
with the exercises and exit checks.

## Conventions

Several textbook formulas differ slightly; this course always uses the
following (see also the [glossary](modules/glossary.qmd)).

| Question | Convention | Excel |
|---|---|---|
| Quartiles and percentiles | Position $(n+1)\times p$ with interpolation | `QUARTILE.EXC`, `PERCENTILE.EXC` |
| Variance and standard deviation | Sample formulas ($n-1$) by default | `VAR.S`, `STDEV.S` |
| Skewness | Adjusted Fisher–Pearson coefficient | `SKEW` |
| Kurtosis | Conceptual only: no formula | — |
| Excel function names | English locale; French names on the [functions page](modules/excel-functions.qmd) | — |
